Subject: Bandwidth & SLO decision pathways — post-call recap and technical asks

Thanks Aman & Priya — quick recap from our call this morning and the immediate asks so we can produce a concrete decision runbook. Nice to meet you both.

Key pain points you shared
- Latency spikes during morning and end-of-day peaks (p95 spikes to ~800ms today).
- Cost unpredictability during heavy inference (batching / autoscale behavior unclear).
- High KV cache miss rate for multi-turn sessions (impacting tail latency).
- Need for strict P95 SLO for user-facing completions and a cost target for per-1k requests.

Goals you stated
- Target p95 <= 220ms for 512-token completions (interactive UI).
- Sustain 600 req/s peak with graceful degradation under 1,000 req/s.
- Data control: option to start on Hosted API, then evaluate Private/VPC for regulated workloads.
- Timeline: pilot in Q1 2027, production by end of Q2 2027.

What we propose as two decision pathways
1) Fast path — Redwood Hosted + Dedicated capacity
   - Dedicated GPU pool with burst capacity and autoscaling policies.
   - Prefix/KV caching tuned to your session patterns; goal warm-hit >= 70%.
   - Model variant routing: high-throughput model for bulk inference; low-latency variant for UI-critical paths.

2) Controlled-private path — Redwood Private (VPC) with model quantization
   - Bring-your-VPC deployment with KMS integration and private control plane.
   - Quantized model variants (int8 / int4) for cost-sensitive batched workloads.
   - Ops playbook for cold-start mitigation and warm pool sizing.

Immediate asks (what we need from VelocityGuard)
- Sample traffic (JSON) with per-request sequence lengths and timestamped rates (attach sample-traffic.json).
- Current measured p50/p95 for the slowest endpoints and a list of top 10 slow queries.
- Expected SLA / business impact table (which endpoints are UI-critical vs batch).
- Any security evidence contact (SOC2 / compliance) so we can scope Private deployment requirements.

Attachments: I attached a short SLO profiling CSV (vg-slo-profiles.csv) and a rough KV-cache sketch (kv-cache-sketch.png) that captures where cache misses are likely happening. I'll follow with a one-page decision runbook and a low-level topology sketch after we get your sample traffic.

Next steps
- VelocityGuard to share sample-traffic.json + p50/p95 snapshots by Wed 11/4.
- Redwood to produce a decision runbook (hosted vs private) and a cost-latency projection by Fri 11/6.
- Schedule technical deep-dive to walk the runbook and sizing assumptions — proposing Tue 11/10 10:00am PT.

Thanks again — Karthik

Aman / Priya — thanks for the details. Below I sketched two concrete topology options with sizing + expected tradeoffs so you can pick a decision pathway. I kept numbers conservative to avoid optimistic gaps in the tail.

Option A — Hosted + Dedicated pool (fastest to production)- Target: p95 <= 220ms for 512 tokens- Pool: 8 x H100-style nodes (template: 80GB GPU) with continuous batching window tuned to 8-12 tokens per batch for UI traffic- KV cache: prefix caching with 30s TTL; expect warm-hit >= 65% after steady-state; recommend 2x memory replicate for high availability- Autoscale: maintain a 20% warm buffer; burst to 12 nodes for peak (600->1,000 req/s)- Model variants: use a low-latency tuned 13B variant for UI, and a quantized 7B for bulk processing (cost fallback)- Expected infra delta: p95 headroom margin ~40-60ms; per-1k request cost estimate (hosted) ~ $X (will refine with traffic).

Option B — Private (VPC) with quantized backfill (best for control & long-term cost)- Target: similar SLOs but with tighter cost control through int8/int4 quantization for batched workloads- Pool: 10 x A100/80GB equivalent for mixed workloads; maintain a dedicated warm pool for UI-serving GPUs (2-3 nodes) to reduce cold-starts- KV cache: local in-VPC Redis with KV sharding aligned to session keys; aim for warm-hit >= 75% (harder initially but better long-term)- Deployment: canary rollout by customer org (can integrate with your CI), automated fallback routing to hosted if private capacity is saturated- Ops: additional runbook steps for KMS/HSM key rotation and audit logging (we'll provide templates).

Technical asks to finalize sizing
- Confirm your acceptable p95 target for 1,100-token tail requests (is graceful degradation acceptable for that tier?).
- Share sample-traffic.json (fields: timestamp, endpoint, seq_len, user_type, latency) — we'll run a synthetic replay to validate batch sizing assumptions.
- Tell us which endpoints require strict UI p95 vs which can be queued to cheaper path.

Quick notes on implementation details we plan to validate during a follow-up deep-dive
- Batching windows: tradeoff between p95 and throughput. We'll test 8ms vs 25ms batching windows.- KV cache TTL tuning and pre-warming strategies for nightly jobs.- Model quantization tests for quality regression (we run automatic evals tied to your prompt set).

I'll compile a short decision tree (Hosted vs Private) and a cost/latency table for Karthik to share Monday with your leadership. Propose a technical replay session after we receive sample-traffic.json — we can do a 90-minute session with ops and infra folks.

-Sean
